title: Dashboard operator UX mapping - compact spec
content:
Purpose and scope:

This compact spec documents a pragmatic mapping between operator workflows (what an engineer does during an incident) and dashboard surface patterns (panels, drill paths, and trace links). Focus is on low-friction investigations for inference infra (latency, kv-cache, model routing, and cost spikes). The goal: make the primary investigative gestures as one- or two-click ops across desktop and mobile.

Why UX matters for observability:
- Incidents are time pressure: reduce cognitive load and handoffs.
- Operators often work from chat/phone: compact views and keyboard shortcuts speed triage.
- Drilling should preserve context (session id, tenant id, model id) across panels and into traces/logs.

Primary operator gestures (ranked):
1) Surface check (0–10s): glance key health, error rate, P95 latency, active queue depth.
2) Filter by tenant/session (10–60s): apply tenant selector and inspect top-of-stack panels.
3) Root-cause pivot (1–10min): pivot between model routing, KV hit-rate, GPU saturation, fallback spikes.
4) Trace dive (3–30min): jump from offending request sample to full trace with annotated model hops.
5) Action and follow-up (5–60min): kick a rollback, open a ticket, annotate timeline.

Dashboard layout recommendations (compact operator edition):
- Top strip (always visible): global filters (time range quick-set, region, environment, tenant id, model family, route). Keep to 1 row.
- Left column (quick triage): 3 small cards: 1) System health summary (boolean icons + small sparklines), 2) SLO status + budget remaining, 3) Alerts & active incidents.
- Main grid (investigation panels): 6 slots (2x3) by default on desktop; collapse to 2x2 on narrow screens. Panels are specialized, not generic.
- Right rail (context & actions): request sampling table (top slow/errored sessions), trace quick-links, recent deployments on top. Rail should pin when a sample is selected.

Panel types and metric contracts (compact definitions):
1) Top-level latency tile
   - Metric name: inference.request.latency_ms
   - Primary aggregate: p50/p95/p99 (ms) over request count (count_nonzero)
   - Tags: tenant_id, model_id, route, region, quantization_profile
   - Drill: click a quantile to open latency-slice panel filtered to that quantile range
2) KV cache warmth panel
   - Metric: kvcache.lookup.hit_rate (0..1) and kvcache.prefetch.misses
   - Units: fraction and counts per minute
   - Contract: must expose per-tenant and per-model shard dimensions
   - UX: show heatmap of model_id vs tenant cohort; click cell -> show sample requests and trace links
3) Model routing fanout panel
   - Metric: routing.fanout.count and routing.fallback.count
   - UX: graph of fanout distribution, stacked by model variant; clicking variant drills into node-level CPU/GPU usage
4) Cost-weighted error map (unique UX)
   - Metric: token_cost.usd_per_token * error.rate -> derived "cost-of-errors"
   - Purpose: prioritize regressions that drive dollars lost; table sorted by cost impact
   - Action: button to snapshot query and open rollback/mitigation issue template
5) Active traces sampler (compact table)
   - Columns: timestamp, tenant_id, session_id, model_id, latency_ms, error_code, trace_link
   - Sampling rule: surface top 50 slowest or errored in last 5m aggregated by tenant weight
6) Deployment overlay (timeline)
   - Pulls deployment events (git sha, model version, rollout %).
   - Contract: events tagged with rollout_policy and expected_impact; clicking event scopes other panels to pre/post window

Keyboard and gesture mapping (operator shortcuts):
- G then H -> Go to Home/Overview
- / -> focus global filter (type to search tenant or model)
- J / K -> jump next/prev sample in Active traces table
- Enter on sample -> open trace modal
- Shift+Click latency tile -> open latency heatmap and apply quantile filter
- C -> create Incident (prefills context: selected tenant, sample id, dashboard permalink)

Mobile / narrow-screen pattern rules:
- Collapse left column into top hamburger summary; quick actions (ack, mute, create incident) must be reachable in one tap
- Use condensed sparklines and short text; hide verbose legends by default
- Active sample modal should be full-screen with big tappable trace button and copy-id icon

Trace integration notes (how panels link to traces):
- Trace snippets must include model hop annotations: {hop_index, model_id, shard, token_range, kv_hit}
- Trace links open lightweight trace viewer with pre-applied filters (focus span = slowest model hop).
- When opening traces from a tenant-scoped dashboard, include tenant_id in trace query to avoid cross-tenant session leakage.
- For privacy: redact user prompt payloads; trace viewer shows only lengths and anonymized prompt fingerprints unless user has explicit audit role.

Investigation flows (example 3-step):
1) Surface check: Home -> latency tile shows p95 jump -> click p95
2) Drill: latency-slice panel -> shows model X increased p95; click model X cell to open KV warmth and routing panels filtered to model X
3) Root cause: KV warmth shows drop in hit_rate -> open top sample -> trace shows repeated kv misses during prefix warmup -> mitigation: enable prefetch for model X or roll back quantization change

Alert design & actionability guidance:
- Alerts must include a short "why this matters" blurb and suggested first action (e.g., "check kv cache warmth -> toggle prefetch" or "scale dedicated pool").
- Avoid noisy p50-based alerts; target p95/p99 or error-rate bursts normalized by tenant weight.
- Attach dashboard permalink and top 3 implicated metrics to the alert payload.

Observability ergonomics playbook (quick checklist for dashboard authors):
- Ensure all panels have at most 3 interactive drill actions (avoid explosion)
- Persist filter state in URL/hash for easy permalink + Slack sharing
- Default time-range for operator views: 15m with quick presets 5m/1h/6h
- Annotate panels with instrumentation provenance (metric source: exporter, histogram buckets used, sampling rate)
- Add a "notes" widget in right rail for chronic incidents and runbook links

Implementation notes and tech tasks (open items):
- [ ] Add quantile-click handler in dashboard framework (frontend task) - JIRA: OBS-1257
- [ ] Backend: expose kvcache shard-level hit_rate with tenant tag - API: /metrics/kvcache?group_by=tenant,shard
- [ ] Trace: add hop annotations (kv_hit, model_chunk_index) in tracing pipeline - PR: repo/observability-dashboards#42
- [ ] Mobile: design condensed tile components and quick-action sheet - UX spike: Maya to prototype

Metrics ownership and SLAs (operational guidance):
- inference.request.latency_ms -> owner: eng-serving-runtime; alert threshold owner-defined; SLO owner should be product-hosted-api
- kvcache.lookup.hit_rate -> owner: platform-engineering; important for cold-start SLOs

Feedback & iteration plan:
- Run a 2-week pilot with oncall squad (rotation 3) using compact operator dashboard as primary investigation tool
- Capture: time-to-first-action, handoff rate, number of drill actions per incident
- Iterate UI based on quantitative feedback and 10 qualitative interviews

Appendix: sample queries (prometheus-like and SQL pseudocode)
- latency p95 (prom): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, tenant_id, model_id))
- kv hit rate (sql): select tenant_id, model_id, sum(hits)/nullif(sum(lookups),0) as hit_rate from kv_metrics where ts > now()-interval '15 minutes' group by tenant_id, model_id order by hit_rate asc limit 50

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact and operator-focused; not a full dashboard spec. Comments welcome on prioritization of gestures and any missing drill paths.
- If we proceed, I'll convert to a clickable prototype and add example panels to the dashboard repo.
